column3: This process map covers phases commonly involved in an arbitration or expert determination, ie a dispute submitted by agreement of the parties to one or more arbitrators or experts who can bindingly decide on the merits. It aims to be relevant across different arbitration and expert determination systems and styles, and across national traditions, so as to enable them to be handled and analysed in a like-for-like way. This wide range has design implications — in particular, a relatively small number of phases not separated out in a system-specific way. The phases are the same as those of the parent process map (Binding Dispute Resolution) on which this process map is based, but with arbitration-specific content.

Covers exchange of information and positions before arbitration, initiation of arbitration, exchange of claims and responses, and establishment of the tribunal. Open statements of a party's legal position are included here; settlement proposals are excluded (see Settlement phase). Procedural failures at commencement belong here; disputes about jurisdiction or validity of the arbitration agreement belong in Related proceedings. Initial pleadings are included here; subsequent rounds belong in Pleadings and evidence.

Where the process provides for a summary resolution of some or all of the merits, that falls into this phase rather than Case management.

column3: Covers challenges to the bringing of proceedings, challenges to arbitral appointments, challenges to awards or decisions, and enforcement of awards or decisions. Challenges to jurisdiction and to the validity of the arbitration agreement are included here, whether brought in the arbitration itself or in a court. If a challenge brought in court is likely to be complex, consider opening a separate matter or sub-matter with its own phases.
